monthly_review.summary: You've increased intensity and pace significantly this month while maintaining cadence, but aerobic efficiency and volume have declined compared to last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Your April average pace improved by 38 sec/km despite a 7 bpm higher average heart rate — indicating meaningful neuromuscular and metabolic adaptation, but at the cost of reduced volume and recovery margin.

goal_tracker.message: You need 12.6 more km across 3 additional sessions (avg 4.2 km/session) in the remaining 18 days to match March’s volume — e.g., add one 5km Zone 2 run, one 4km tempo-adjacent run, and one 4km easy run.

insights.title: Efficiency gain despite higher HR
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency improved from 13.28 to 13.62 (+0.34) even as avg HR rose +7 bpm — suggesting better oxygen utilization per stride, likely driven by recent faster efforts like the 7:25/km (445 sec/km) best pace on 4/12.

insights.title: Zone 3–4 dominance with minimal Z1 recovery
insights.body: This month, 50% of time was spent in Zones 3–4 (26% Z3 + 24% Z4), up from 48% last month — but Z1 dropped to just 11% (vs 4% in March, though that was likely measurement artifact; still, true recovery volume remains low).

insights.title: Stride length variability correlates with pace and effort
insights.body: Stride length ranged from 70.96 cm (6.2km @ 9:00/km, lowest intensity) to 90.77 cm (5.0km @ 7:25/km, highest HR 163 bpm) — a 28% increase — confirming strong neuromuscular engagement at faster paces, but vertical oscillation stayed stable (7.8–8.5 cm), indicating controlled form.

insights.title: Aerobic TE jumped while volume dropped
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE rose to 3.5 (from 3.0) despite 39% less km and 43% fewer runs — signaling high-intensity density, but with only 4 runs and no Z1 emphasis, cumulative fatigue risk is elevated (evidenced by 11 bpm HR rise from easy run on 4/01 to hard run on 4/12).

recommendations.action: Do a 5km Zone 2 run (HR ≤138 bpm) within next 48 hours, focusing on stride length ≥78 cm and vertical oscillation ≤8.0 cm
recommendations.reason: Your lowest HR run (4/01, 142 bpm, 6.2km) was still above true Zone 2 ceiling (~135–138 bpm for your profile); rebuilding Z1–Z2 volume is critical to sustain TE gains without burnout.

recommendations.action: Repeat the 5.0km session from 4/12 (7:25/km, HR 163 bpm) as a *controlled* 4km Zone 4 interval run: 4 x 1km @ 445–455 sec/km with 90-sec walk recovery
recommendations.reason: That run delivered your highest aerobic TE (4.6) and best stride length (90.77 cm) — structuring it as intervals reduces ground contact stress while preserving neuromuscular benefit.

recommendations.action: Add a 20-min post-run mobility routine targeting hip flexors and calves after every run this week, measured by ground contact time <305 ms in next 2 runs
recommendations.reason: Ground contact averaged 307–311 ms in recent runs — slightly elevated vs optimal for your pace; mobility directly improves elastic recoil and contact time.

weekly_focus.description: Balance the gains from your recent hard efforts with intentional low-HR volume and movement quality — prioritizing HR control, contact time reduction, and neural freshness over pure distance or pace.
